Camille Roux
Full-Stack Engineer
Lyon, France · camille.roux@example.com · https://github.com/example-camille

EXPERIENCE
Full-Stack Engineer, Routeo (B2B logistics SaaS), Lyon · Jan 2022 – present
- Build features across a TypeScript / Node.js (NestJS) back end and a React front end for a shipment-booking platform.
- Designed an event-driven billing pipeline with RabbitMQ that processes about 50,000 invoices a month.
- Own PostgreSQL schema changes and query tuning; cut the slowest report from 40 s to 3 s.
- Run services on AWS (ECS, RDS, SQS) with Docker and Terraform; on call one week a month.
- Write unit and integration tests with Jest and Playwright; mentor two junior developers.

Junior Web Developer, Atelier Lumen (web agency), Lyon · Sep 2020 – Dec 2021
- Built React and Node.js websites and back offices for more than 10 clients.

EDUCATION
Master's degree in Computer Science, Lyon · 2018 – 2020

SKILLS
TypeScript, JavaScript, Node.js, NestJS, React, PostgreSQL, RabbitMQ, AWS, Docker, Terraform, Jest, Playwright
Languages: French (native), English (fluent, C1)
jobText:
Full-Stack Engineer
Veloria · Remote within the European Union · Full-time

Veloria is a Paris-based company that builds invoicing and payment software for European freelancers. 40,000 freelancers use us every month.

Your mission
- Build product features across our TypeScript back end and React front end.
- Own services end to end: design, tests, deployment and monitoring.

Must have
- 3+ years of professional experience as a full-stack engineer.
- TypeScript and Node.js on the back end.
- React on the front end.
- PostgreSQL.
- Automated testing (unit and integration tests).
- Experience with message queues (RabbitMQ, Kafka or SQS).
- Running services on AWS in production.
- Professional English.

Nice to have
- French.
- Docker.
- GraphQL.

Location
Remote within the European Union. You must already have the right to work in the EU: we cannot sponsor visas. We meet in Paris twice a year (travel paid).

Salary: 55,000–70,000 EUR + equity.
